note: Re-judged 2026-10-20 (independent judge, after d6e44c3bb1). Section 4.4.1: "Every SPD SHOULD have a nominal, final entry that matches anything that is otherwise unmatched, and discards it." The only cited producer that moved is warnSPDLeft: d6e44c3bb1 changed the warning message only (entries named by their exact `ip xfrm policy delete` command, so the port 500 and port 4500 IKE bypasses are distinguishable). Return semantics unchanged: true iff the ledger holds an entry, and releaseSPD then skips removeUnmatched, so the discard catch-all stays beneath every leftover Ze entry. removeZePolicy, installUnmatched, unmatchedPolicies, parseUnmatched, applyConfig and shutdown are unchanged. The three tagged carriers are unchanged in body: TestRFC4301DefaultFinalSPDEntryDiscards (with the leaf absent, the last entry in every direction and family is a wildcard discard), TestRFC4301FinalEntryIsUnderEveryZeSPDEntry (replays every recorded write through apply, a Child SA and shutdown, failing the moment any Ze entry is live without the discard catch-all), and TestRFC4301InboundClearPacketIsDiscardedByTheDefaultFinalEntry (real XFRM, a clear inbound packet matching no other entry is dropped). All pass at HEAD together with TestReleaseSPDKeepsTheCatchAllWhenARemovalFails, TestChildInstallRollbackFailureIsRecordedInTheSPDLedger and TestSPDLeftoverNamesTheExactRemovalCommand. Scope note carried from RFC4301-5.2-1: VPP holds no catch-all and the OSPFv3 RFC 4552 entries have none; those are the disclosed gap there and do not touch the SPD Ze's IKE engine builds, which these tests pin. Verdict stands.
